To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lipid content of calanoid copepod species varies significantly across depth differences as fine as 12–20 m in the photic layer of the Red Sea and the Mediterranean Sea.
the lipid content of individual calanoids of the same species can differ significantly among depth layers within the photic zone.
Lipids in calanoid copepod individuals of the same species and life stage/sex can vary significantly across depth differences as narrow as 12–20 meters within the photic zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the vertical distribution of calanoid copepod species, and their lipid content, in relation to the physical environment.
the question: How does lipid content vary among individuals of the same species and life stage within the photic zone of the upper water column in the Red Sea, the Mediterranean Sea and the Arctic?
the vertical distribution of copepod species and the lipid content in different depth ranges within the photic zone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

lipid content of calanoid copepod individuals of the same species can vary significantly within the photic zone and that these intraspecific differences are more pronounced in warm oligotrophic waters.
lipid content of calanoid copepod species varies with depth within the photic zone and that this variation is species-specific.

lipid content in copepods is not a constant within the photic zone and that the differences in lipid contents across small depth ranges are not only due to differences in food availability, but also to the avoidance of predators and/or buoyancy regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the depth range of a species is not a single value, but rather a continuum, and individuals of the same species may have different lipid contents at different depths.
lipid content in some calanoid copepod species may be related to the vertical distribution of the species and the presence of predators.
lipid content is not a simple function of depth, but is also dependent on species, sex, life stage, temperature, food availability, and possibly other environmental factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even within a narrow depth range within the photic zone, individuals of the same species may differ in lipid content and this should be taken into consideration in future research on copepods.
lipid content in calanoid copepod individuals of the same species can differ significantly between fine depth ranges within the photic zone.
lipid content of the same copepod species can vary significantly across depth ranges of a few meters.
